title: Regulatory Export Orchestrator — verifiable bundles, regional retention rules, & delivery SLAs
creator: Sonia Patel
description:
Problem: Customers need a robust, tenant-scoped export orchestration service that can produce signed, verifiable export bundles (PDF/CSV) on a schedule, respect per-tenant residency & retention policies, and deliver artifacts to tenant destinations with SLA/graceful-fallback behavior. Current ad-hoc exports lack verification manifests, have brittle delivery retries, and do not consistently apply regional retention rules or timezone-aware scheduling.

Goal: Design and ship a Compliance Export Orchestrator that: (1) runs scheduled snapshot exports per tenant and per-region, (2) emits cryptographically verifiable bundles (manifest + SHA256 + PAdES-signed PDFs where required), (3) supports configurable CSV schemas and locale-aware formatting, (4) routes deliveries to tenant destinations (S3, secure SFTP, or signed download link) with per-delivery expiry and retry/backoff policies, and (5) enforces retention/auto-delete policies post-export and records auditable evidence entries in the compliance ledger.

Scope: This ticket covers product requirements, delivery SLA presets, acceptance criteria, tenant UX for scheduling, and orchestration behavior. Engineering tickets will implement export worker, signer service integration, delivery adapters, and retention enforcement. Design will provide export bundle UX and manifest display in Console.

Out of scope: transformation/normalization of unstructured customer data beyond CSV/PDF mapping, long-term cold storage lifecycle management (handled by storage tiering roadmap).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Tenants can create scheduled export jobs in Console with frequency, timezone, destination type, and retention enforcement selected.
2) Each completed export contains: (a) a machine-readable manifest.json (SHA256 checksums), (b) human-friendly PDF bundle that is optionally PAdES-signed, (c) CSV datasets following selected schema templates.
3) Export manifest is signed by Redwood's export-signing key and verifiable by customer via SHA256 + signature.
4) Delivery options: S3 (cross-region aware with presigned object expiry), secure SFTP, or single-use signed download link; delivery status surfaceable in Console with timestamps and retries.
5) Per-tenant residency and retention rules are applied: if tenant policy requires delete-after-export, an automated retention job will remove exported records from active storage after configured window and record the action in audit log.
6) SLA tiers (Standard/Expedited) are selectable; SLA violations trigger alerts to CSM/Support and generate incident tickets automatically.
7) Dashboard shows export history, success/failure rates, bytes exported, and per-tenant cost estimate.
8) Security review completed and documented; signing keys integrated with KMS/HSM and rotation plan exists.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Kickoff: PM, Eng, and Design alignment meeting. Agreed to support both PAdES-signed PDFs and unsigned PDFs behind tenant toggle.
2026-03-03 - Engineering (Eng lead @Maya Singh): proposed worker model with idempotent job keys and visibility into partial failures. Raised need for KMS-backed signing API (dependency ENG-2145).
2026-03-05 - Design (Alex Chen): initial Console mocks uploaded; UX will expose 'retention after export' as a toggle with preflight warnings for irreversible deletes.
2026-03-08 - PM decision: include multi-schema CSV selection and locale-aware number/date formatting per tenant (currency and timezone-aware).
2026-03-10 - Security: draft threat model reviewed. Must use HSM for signing and ensure manifests are immutable once published.
2026-03-12 - Blocker identified: cross-region SFTP delivery requires network egress exception in EMEA private deployments (logged ENG-2212).
